record.original_question: Can the Madelung-transform results identifying symplectomorphism and Kahler map structures be extended to wave functions with zeros on M, and can the quantization-condition controversy be explained through the momentum map for the semidirect product of diffeomorphisms and smooth functions?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $M$ be a closed Riemannian manifold, and consider the space $\mathcal{W}(M)$ of complex-valued wave functions $\psi:M\to\mathbb{C}$ of fixed $L^2$-norm. Let $\mathrm{Dens}(M)$ denote the space of smooth probability densities on $M$, equipped with the Fisher–Rao information metric, and let $T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$ be its cotangent bundle. The Madelung transform sends a nowhere-vanishing wave function $\psi = \sqrt{\rho}\,e^{i\theta/\hbar}$ to the pair $(\rho,\theta)\in T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$ (modulo a global phase). It is known that, restricted to nowhere-vanishing wave functions, the Madelung transform is a symplectomorphism and indeed a Kähler isometry (with respect to the Fubini–Study metric on $\mathcal{W}(M)$ and the Sasaki-type metric induced from Fisher–Rao on $T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$); moreover, it arises as the momentum map of the natural action of the semidirect product group $\mathrm{Diff}(M)\ltimes C^\infty(M,\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathcal{W}(M)$.

(a) Extend these results — the symplectomorphism property, the Kähler isometry property, and the momentum-map interpretation — to the full space $\mathcal{W}(M)$ including wave functions with zeros, identifying the appropriate target space (a suitable completion or stratified extension of $T^*\mathrm{Dens}(M)$) on which the extended Madelung map is well defined.

(b) Using the momentum-map structure for the semidirect product $\mathrm{Diff}(M)\ltimes C^\infty(M,\mathbb{R})$, give a geometric explanation of the quantization condition on the circulation $\oint d\theta \in 2\pi\hbar\,\mathbb{Z}$ that arises around zeros of $\psi$, and clarify the apparent controversy concerning whether such a condition must be imposed.
artifact.status_search_result: The Kähler/symplectomorphism property and momentum-map interpretation of the Madelung transform are established for nowhere-vanishing wave functions in works by Khesin–Misiołek–Modin (2019) and Fusca (2017). The full extension to wave functions with zeros and a geometric resolution of the quantization-condition issue via the semidirect product momentum map do not appear to have been completed in the literature; the problem remains open as far as could be verified.

status_evidence.title: Geometry of the Madelung Transform
status_evidence.snippet: The Madelung transform is a Kähler map between wave functions and the cotangent bundle to the density space with the Fubini-Study and Fisher–Rao metrics.
status_evidence.claim: Kähler/symplectomorphism property established for nowhere-vanishing wave functions.

status_evidence.title: The Madelung Transform as a Momentum Map
status_evidence.snippet: The Madelung transform is shown to be a momentum map for the action of a semidirect product group on wave functions.
status_evidence.claim: Momentum-map structure known in the non-vanishing case.
